country3-usage.title: Countries and directions
country3-usage.body: Like welcher/welches/welche, vilken/vilket/vilka agrees with the noun, but Swedish has two noun genders.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

perfect3-usage.title: Past, perfect and clause order
perfect3-usage.body: Swedish uses har even where German uses sein: har gått. In subordinate clauses the verb does not move to the end.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

people3-usage.title: People and reasons
people3-usage.body: Hur ser hon ut? corresponds to Wie sieht sie aus? Eftersom clauses keep the finite verb after the subject and sentence adverb, rather than last.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

modals3-usage.title: Plans, calls and instructions
modals3-usage.body: Modal verbs do not change with person. Swedish keeps the following infinitive next to the modal more often than German does.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

employment3-usage.title: Work and applications
employment3-usage.body: Relative som does not inflect like der/die/das. The clause keeps ordinary subject–verb order rather than placing the finite verb last.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

environment3-usage.title: Environment and comparison
environment3-usage.body: Än corresponds to als in comparisons. För att + infinitive corresponds to um … zu.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

renting3-usage.title: Renting and housing
renting3-usage.body: Ingen/inget/inga is similar to kein with gender/number agreement. Om corresponds to wenn for a condition.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

traffic3-usage.title: Traffic and journeys
traffic3-usage.body: Swedish short answers often use det + auxiliary + subject. When a subordinate clause comes first, the main clause starts with its finite verb, as in German.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

budget3-usage.title: Bills and a budget
budget3-usage.body: Distinguish låna (leihen, receiving) from låna ut (verleihen, giving). Keep the particle ut with the lending meaning.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

clinic3-usage.title: At the clinic
clinic3-usage.body: Heller corresponds to auch in a negative statement: inte heller, auch nicht. Också is used in positive statements.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

relationships3-usage.title: Relationships and messages
relationships3-usage.body: Att corresponds to dass, but does not send the finite verb to the end. Vilket fint hus! corresponds to Was für ein schönes Haus!

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

society3-usage.title: Politics and public services
society3-usage.body: Både … och corresponds to sowohl … als auch; varken … eller to weder … noch. Subordinate clauses retain Swedish word order.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection
